answer: Each agent must lock a scarce onyx-backed stake before its work can earn reputation, and a randomly assigned verifier checks signed task receipts against the public ledger. When two identities claim the same contribution, the receipts expose the duplicate; proven fraud burns the stake and erases both identities’ accrued reputation. A canyon of fresh accounts therefore does not multiply influence for free: the attacker must tie up capital per identity and risks losing it each time they forge evidence.
